text: {"score":4,"justification":"Numbers match the card (18.0%, 2.9%, 15.66, z 2.18, 58%, 30 claims, 8 documented 99215, 6 of 23). The summary is cautious, explains billed level against complexity, and flags thin documentation. The weaknesses are a few unsupported or loosely supported claims and next steps that are generic compared with the narrative.","problems":["The sampled low-complexity claims are described as 'back pain, rash, abdominal pain, URI or follow-up codes', but no rash code appears on the card (R21 is a rash code, so this is borderline, though it is not obviously a minor problem).","The 'excess holds in every complexity stratum' claim is loosely supported, and 'the 0–1 condition strata carry the largest absolute excess' is not computed on the card.","The statement that notes 'may be templated or inflated' on the basis of 6 claims with no lab line is speculative. Absence of a lab line on a claim does not show that the data review was not done.","The cited claim ids (C0090951, C0090956) are only 1-condition cases such as obesity and type 2 diabetes, which are weaker examples than the 0-condition claims named in the narrative (C0091319, C0091920, etc.). Those narrative claims are not in the cited list.","The next_steps are generic ('larger sample of 99214 and 99215', 're-screen'), and the more specific targeted-chart request and cloned-MDM check appear only in the rationale text rather than in next_steps.","Comparison with the 17% rate for other providers is correct, but the summary does not note that the documented 99215 sample was only 8."]}
